subject.title: Feature Request: Support YAML as config file format

question: Should OpenClaw add YAML/YML as a supported core config-file format, or keep JSON5 `openclaw.json` canonical and invest in config set/patch/docs?
rationale: Current code and docs define one JSON5 config-file contract, while YAML support would add precedence, parser, write-back, reload, doctor, and upgrade behavior that repository policy treats as product-sensitive.

options.title: Keep JSON5 Canonical
options.body: Reaffirm JSON5 `openclaw.json` and steer programmatic edits through `openclaw config` and `config.patch`; close or narrow this issue after that decision is explicit.

options.title: Approve YAML Fallback
options.body: Accept YAML only as a fully specified config contract with `.yaml`/`.yml` precedence, parser semantics, write-back behavior, reload/doctor coverage, docs, and upgrade tests.

options.title: Close As Not Planned
options.body: Declare that OpenClaw will not add a second core config-file format and ask for concrete gaps in config mutation tooling as separate issues.

recommendation.title: Keep JSON5 Canonical
recommendation.body: Reaffirm JSON5 `openclaw.json` and steer programmatic edits through `openclaw config` and `config.patch`; close or narrow this issue after that decision is explicit.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history on the published config docs and config IO safety surface that define this product contract.
